The revival includes a new GitHub repository and a history page crediting prior contributors—a one-person bet on a project that went quiet when its previous stewards moved on." keywords: ["nextbsd returns dollop apple source freebsd"] categories: ["technology"] tags: ["nextbsd returns dollop apple source freebsd", "technology"] references: - id: "theregister-com-ece6258a" type: "webpage" title: "NextBSD returns to dollop Apple source on FreeBSD" URL: "https://www.theregister.com/os-platforms/2026/07/18/nextbsd-returns-to-dollop-apple-source-on-freebsd/5273788" container-title: "theregister.com" issued: date-parts: [[2026, 7, 18]] license: "CC BY 4.0" license_url: "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" syndication_rights: "Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International; Koios.News permits indexing, snippets, large image previews, feed distribution, Google Search/News/Discover surfaces, and other attributed downstream syndication." koios: seo_term: "nextbsd returns dollop apple source freebsd" beat: "technology" gates_clear: false assignment_id: "technology-nextbsd-returns-dollop-apple-source-freebsd-5bce39c6" tweet: "NextBSD Returns Under New Leadership to Resume Porting Apple Source Into FreeBSD" --- After seven years during which the original GitHub repository sat frozen at its last commit, NextBSD has returned to potential development—under new management, with a new repository separate from the original, and the same founding purpose: porting Apple's open-source Darwin code into the FreeBSD ecosystem. [The Register's FOSS desk reported the revival on July 18, 2026.](https://www.theregister.com/os-platforms/2026/07/18/nextbsd-returns-to-dollop-apple-source-on-freebsd/5273788) NextBSD was started in 2015 by Jordan Hubbard, a co-founder of FreeBSD. The plan from the beginning was to port components of Apple's Darwin OS to FreeBSD. Darwin is the Unix foundation on which macOS and Apple's other operating systems are built; it is open source, with its code available directly from GitHub. Bridging that codebase into FreeBSD required sustained porting effort—work that exists only as long as someone is actively doing it. ## NextBSD Returns: Apple Darwin Source Porting Under New FreeBSD Stewardship The developer who revived the project is Joe Maloney, known on GitHub as pkgdemon. Maloney is already recognized in BSD circles: he built the Gershwin desktop environment for GhostBSD, which The Register previously covered. Shortly after that coverage, Maloney approached the NextBSD maintainers and asked if he could take over the project. He had a relatively minor role in the original—his commits are visible in the project's history—and now leads the revived effort. The new GitHub repository is distinct from the archived original, which remains accessible with its history intact. The revived project also includes a project history page that gives credit where it's due, as The Register describes it. ## What Apple Source Integration on FreeBSD Actually Requires NextBSD's specific work is integrating Apple's open-source Darwin components into FreeBSD.
